$comment: Options object for the generic Modbus register-map meter. Its three keys (connector_options/listener_options/controller_options) are spread into ModbusMeter.__init__ by main.create_classes — keep in lockstep with the constructor; tests/test_config.py enforces this. The register map lives here rather than in code so one device class covers many meter models: Modbus standardises the framing and standardises nothing about what lives at which address.

name.$comment: Must reference an existing connector name — enforced by Config at load time, not by the schema

interval.$comment: Poll period in seconds; falls back to the connector's default_interval.

device_id.$comment: This meter's Modbus unit id, overriding the connector's default. The useful level when one TCP gateway fronts several RS-485 slaves.

word_order.$comment: Which 16-bit half of a multi-word value comes first. Declared per device, not per connector: two meters behind one gateway routinely disagree, so it is not a property of the transport.

registers.$comment: One entry per Modbus request. There is deliberately no contiguous-address grouping: meters leave holes in their maps and many answer IllegalDataAddress for the WHOLE PDU when any address in a span is unimplemented, which would turn '11 of 12 registers work' into '0 of 12' and name a synthetic range instead of the register to fix.

name.$comment: The stable metric name, and the join key between the connector's read and this device's decoder. MetricSource forbids positional keys, so this is where naming comes from.

address.$comment: The ZERO-BASED protocol address, not the 4xxxx data-model number. Deliberately never auto-translated: some devices genuinely expose protocol address 40001, so the heuristic would be silently wrong for them.

type.$comment: Which of the four Modbus tables. They are four separate address spaces — address 0 is four different things.

data_type.$comment: How to decode the words. Mirrors pymodbus's DATATYPE member names so a vendor's pymodbus example transfers 1:1, plus RAW for 'hand me the words'. Ignored for coil/discrete, which decode to bool.

count.$comment: Words to read. Defaults from data_type (1/2/4); required for STRING, and the override for a vendor padding a 16-bit value into a 32-bit slot.

scale.$comment: value = raw * scale. A multiplier, matching how datasheets state it ('LSB = 0.01 kWh'), so there is no mental inversion at config time.

unit.$comment: Carried into self.data so a stored reading is self-describing. Never used to convert — see `role`.

device_id.$comment: Per-register unit-id override; the escape hatch for a meter that aggregates a second slave.

role.$comment: How a generic meter knows which register is its kWh total. A closed enum, not free text, so a typo is a config warning rather than a total that silently reports 0.0 for the life of the deployment. It promises the SCALED value is already kWh — no conversion is derived from `unit`, because a typo there would rescale a revenue reading by 1000. Several registers may carry it (a two-tariff meter has T1 and T2); they are summed.

controller_options.$comment: Meaningful only on the modbus_switch kind — a plain modbus_meter is not writable, so Device.control refuses commands before they reach the connector.

on_value.$comment: kind=register only: the value written for the Switch COMMAND_ON token. Set it to a number for a setpoint channel.

scale.$comment: kind=register only: raw = round(command / scale), the inverse of the read path.

signed.$comment: kind=register only: picks the 0..65535 vs -32768..32767 range check.
